item.title: Palau's so-called ties with Taiwan line pockets of a few: foreign ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Palau's so-called ties with Taiwan line pockets of a few: foreign ministry BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- For certain countries like Palau, having Taiwan as a "diplomatic ally" is not about delivering for the country and the people, but to line the pockets of the very few people who profit from it, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a regular press briefing on Monday. Mao made the remarks in response to a query on the recent reports that Taiwan increased its annual aid to Palau from 18 million U.S. dollars last year to 25 million U.S. dollars this year, and it also allocated nearly 281,000 U.S. dollars in direct cash gifts for Palau's former president, incumbent political figures, and individual lawmakers. The report is yet another example of the Lai Ching-te authorities' expensive dollar diplomacy using the hard-earned money of the people in Taiwan, which is a combination of corruption, fraudulence, bribery and power-for-money deals, to serve "Taiwan independence" separatism and their personal political agenda, Mao said.

item.title: Surge in passenger traffic highlights close cross-Strait bonds on 'mini three links' routes
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Surge in passenger traffic highlights close cross-Strait bonds on 'mini three links' routes Passenger traffic on the "mini three links" routes between Taiwan and the mainland surged during the summer vacation, highlighting the close bonds across the Taiwan Strait, a mainland spokeswoman said Wednesday. Zhang Han, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, noted that the strong performance of these routes reflects the deep connections between people on both sides of the Strait. The ferry routes, connecting coastal areas in Fujian province with the islands of Jinmen and Matsu, are crucial for travel and exchanges between the mainland and Taiwan. During the summer, the Xiamen-Jinmen route alone operated 1,550 ferries, accommodating 386,400 passenger trips — an increase of 11.4 percent and 24.1 percent year-on-year, respectively. On Aug 23, daily passenger trips on this route exceeded 7,900, the highest since operations resumed in 2023. To manage the increased traffic, mainland authorities enhanced service capacity by extending operating hours, streamlining customs procedures, strengthening maritime safety, and improving passenger services. Smart systems were also implemented to ensure efficient and smooth clearance. Zhang emphasized that the "mini three links" routes have been operating safely and efficiently, and she encouraged more people from Taiwan to travel to the mainland using these routes.

item.title: Mainland condemns Taiwan's increased 'defense' budget
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Mainland condemns Taiwan's increased 'defense' budget A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday condemned the Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for escalating cross-Strait tensions by increasing the island's "defense" budget, reaffirming the mainland's unwavering resolve to combat "Taiwan independence" separatist activities. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference, saying that Lai's authorities have stubbornly adhered to a separatist stance while disregarding the mainstream public aspiration for exchanges, cooperation, development and peace in Taiwan. Recently, the Democratic Progressive Party authorities proposed raising Taiwan's annual "defense" budget to more than NT$1 trillion ($31.4 billion) in 2027, surpassing that threshold for the first time. Lai claimed the move aims to ensure that "defense" resources are transformed into "reliable defensive capabilities". Zhang accused the authorities of escalating cross-Strait confrontation and squandering public resources in a futile attempt to "resist reunification by force" and pursue "Taiwan independence" through force. "They are utterly overestimating their capabilities and will only bring severe disaster to the people of Taiwan," she said. Zhang reiterated that the mainland's resolve and ability to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity are unwavering and strong, leaving no room for any form of "Taiwan independence" separatist activities. "We hope that Taiwan compatriots recognize the harm and danger of 'Taiwan independence' separatism, firmly oppose such separatist actions, and steadfastly uphold the common homeland of the Chinese nation as well as their own safety and well-being," Zhang added.

item.title: Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities' move to increase defense spending
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities' move to increase defense spending BEIJING -- A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday criticized the decision of Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te to raise the island's defense budget in 2027, saying it would only bring grave disaster to the people in Taiwan. Zhang Han, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a question about the island's defense budget of more than NT$1 trillion (about $31 billion) for 2027, which Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te said was aimed at strengthening its defense capabilities and demonstrating its resolve to defend itself. Zhang said Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te have stubbornly adhered to their separatist stance of seeking "Taiwan independence," disregarding the mainstream public opinion on the island that calls for "peace, development, cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation." They have instead stoked confrontation across the Taiwan Strait and squandered public funds in pursuit of their independence agenda, Zhang said, adding that such efforts are "simply beyond their capabilities" and will only have serious consequences for the people of Taiwan. "We are unwavering in our resolve and formidable in our ability to safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and will never leave any room for separatist activities seeking 'Taiwan independence' in any form," Zhang noted. She called on people in Taiwan to recognize the dangers of "Taiwan independence" separatism, firmly oppose such activities, and safeguard the common home of the Chinese nation. Taiwan's executive authorities approved the island's 2027 general budget on Aug 20, with defense spending rising sharply to over NT$1 trillion for the first time. The defense budget accounts for roughly 29 percent of total government expenditure, meaning that about 29 out of every 100 New Taiwan dollars in government spending would go toward defense.

item.title: Economic Watch: Cross-Strait semiconductor firms eye cooperation, new opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
Economic Watch: Cross-Strait semiconductor firms eye cooperation, new opportunities TAIPEI, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Chinese mainland and Taiwan semiconductor companies taking part in SEMICON Taiwan 2026 -- a world-leading specialized semiconductor exhibition -- expressed their willingness to pool complementary strengths and embrace new opportunities. The three-day exhibition concluded on Friday at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center. Organized by the global semiconductor industry association SEMI, the annual event was first held in September 1996, covering the entire semiconductor supply chain, including equipment, materials, packaging and testing. This year it brought together more than 1,300 exhibitors and hosted over 4,300 booths. A number of mainland companies attended the exhibition and presented their latest products, offering a glimpse of the potential to share new opportunities in the rapidly evolving semiconductor industry on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. At the booth of Huangshan Juxin New Material Co., Ltd., samples of materials in various sizes and colors were neatly displayed, drawing inquiries from Taiwan industry professionals. "Many Taiwan companies have shown strong interest in our products, and some visitors are friends we met at last year's exhibition," said Qu Chao, the company's sales director. The high-tech company, which specializes in high-performance polyimide materials, was attending the exhibition for the second time. "Polyimide materials are used throughout the semiconductor industry, from front-end chip manufacturing to back-end packaging," Qu said, adding that Juxin's products offer competitive prices, customized services and full traceability. "There is considerable room for greater cross-Strait industrial cooperation," Qu said, adding that with Taiwan possessing a well-developed semiconductor supply chain, materials from mainland suppliers could be further processed by local companies and applied across a wider range of fields. At the booth of Taiwan-based Veego Corporation, anti-reflective optical windows and gold-coated quartz panels were displayed under bright lights. The products were manufactured by Lianyungang Huide Quartz Glass Co., Ltd., and were being exhibited in Taiwan for the first time through Veego Corporation. "We are optimistic about the quality and potential of mainland quartz products," said Chuang Ya-hui of Veego Corporation, noting that the two companies established their partnership last year, hoping to introduce the products to more Taiwan customers and explore additional applications. Other mainland exhibitors also used the event to explore more advanced forms of industrial cooperation. Anchu Technology Co., Ltd., based in the eastern Chinese city of Zhangjiagang, specializes in formulated functional electronic chemicals and the safe storage of electronic specialty gases for semiconductor manufacturing. The company brought its flagship product -- a negative-pressure gas cylinder designed for the safe storage of high-purity electronic gases -- to this year's exhibition. "We believe the product has strong competitiveness in the Taiwan market," said Jing Shaoqing, the company's marketing director. Anchu Technology has participated in the exhibition for three consecutive years and consistently received enthusiastic inquiries from Taiwan businesses, Jing said. The exhibition came as Taiwan's semiconductor industry faces growing pressure to expand production overseas, particularly in the United States, as industrial insiders warned of a broader U.S. strategy to establish a whole supply chain that increasingly sidelines Taiwan. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), the world's leading contract chipmaker and a cornerstone of Taiwan's technology industry, has become a central focus of those efforts. The company has announced massive investments in Arizona, while its suppliers in Taiwan are also facing increasing pressure to expand operations in the United States. Against this backdrop, industry observers are calling for diversifying markets and strengthening industrial links. "The two sides of the Strait have strong complementarities in terms of semiconductor applications and markets," said Lo Huai-jia, secretary-general of the Taiwan R&D Managers Association. Noting that the mainland is one of the world's most important manufacturing bases, Lo said as its manufacturing sector continues to develop, demand for semiconductor products and the range of their applications are also expected to expand. "The complementary strengths of industries on both sides of the Strait could create much broader room for cooperation," Lo added.

item.title: Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang Organizes Compatriots and Families of Taiwan Origin to Experience Intangible Cultural Heritage
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang Organizes Compatriots and Families of Taiwan Origin to Experience Intangible Cultural Heritage Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-04
Sep 4(Taiwan.cn)—On August 27, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Xingyang organized representatives of Taiwan compatriots and their family members residing locally to take part in an immersive observation？and？experience activity featuring intangible cultural heritage. During the event, participants visited distinctive cultural sites including the Chang？style Boxing Training Institute, the Yellow River Chengni Inkstone Art Museum, and the Hou？dian Village Hollow？out Cultural and Creative Park to learn about the preservation and inheritance of local intangible cultural heritage resources. With on？site briefings, craft demonstrations and interactive hands？on sessions, Taiwan compatriots and their families gained detailed insights into the historical evolution, inheritance lineage, technical features and inheritance system of each intangible cultural heritage item. Rooted in Xingyang’s local intangible cultural heritage resources, the activity allowed Taiwan compatriots and their families to get close？up exposure to the profound heritage and humanistic spirit of traditional martial arts, craftsmanship and folk arts. It further deepened their understanding of the historical bonds that bind people across the Taiwan Strait as one origin with shared culture and ethnicity. item.title: China completes marine geophysical survey in waters east of its Taiwan Island
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
China completes marine geophysical survey in waters east of its Taiwan Island Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China conducted a comprehensive marine geophysical survey in waters east of its Taiwan Island from Aug. 10 to 31, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Thursday. The survey, carried out by the Second Institute of Oceanography under the ministry, was aimed at gaining a comprehensive understanding of the basic geological conditions and seabed structural features of waters under China's jurisdiction, and supporting the development of a digital platform for natural resources administration and territorial-spatial planning. It collected basic data on the seabed environment, including seafloor topography, sedimentary strata, deep geological structures and geophysical fields. The data will help China further understand the seabed geological and geophysical characteristics of this area, and provide data for geological research on seabed sedimentation and tectonic structures, as well as deep crustal structure and geodynamic evolution in waters east of Taiwan Island, according to the ministry. The survey also provides a scientific basis for China's integrated governance of waters under its jurisdiction in the region. Related Stories

item.title: Comment on Taiwan TV draws criticism on both sides of the Strait
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
Comment on Taiwan TV draws criticism on both sides of the Strait A comment made on a Taiwan TV program claiming that "there are no refrigerators in Beijing" has drawn criticism on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. "Such remarks, which are detached from reality, will only make a laughingstock of themselves," Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular news conference on Wednesday. She said the Democratic Progressive Party authorities have imposed restrictions on and obstructed cross-Strait exchanges and interactions, deliberately creating an "information cocoon" on the island in an attempt to prevent Taiwan residents from learning about the mainland. "We welcome Taiwan residents to break through these barriers, visit the mainland more often and see for themselves the real and vibrant mainland," Zhang said. On a Taiwan TV program called Newswawawa, Liao Mei-ran, a self-described "fortune teller", claimed that during a visit to the mainland, she found "there were no refrigerators in Beijing, and people in Beijing did not have cold drinks". The remark drew attention on both sides of the Strait. Some Taiwan netizens said it reflected the extent to which the island has become an "information cocoon". "While it may appear that you are mocking the mainland, in fact, it is Taiwan that is embarrassing itself," one commenter wrote.

item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.
